headline: Seven majors under their 200-day lines, but ETFs keep buying and shorts keep getting squeezed
paragraphs: Start with structure: every asset on the board, BTC through ADA, sits below its 200-day moving average, and none show a golden cross. BTC trades $64,915, itself 48% off its 12-month high. The rest are deeper underwater: ETH -60.2%, XRP -68.4%, SOL -69.3%, BNB -54.1%, DOGE -75.7%, ADA -79.3%. That is a market recovering from a broad drawdown across the board, not one laggard surrounded by leaders.

Momentum is more mixed than the trend picture. RSI readings cluster in the mid-50s to mid-60s for BTC, ETH, SOL and BNB, which is firm but not stretched, while XRP sits weak at 38.5 and DOGE at 45. MACD is bullish (above signal) for BTC, SOL, BNB, DOGE and ADA, but bearish for ETH and XRP. ETH is the notable divergence: up 22.41% over 30 days, yet its MACD sits below signal, momentum cooling even as price has climbed. ADA is the outlier on the other side, up 22.93% over 7 days and 38.7% over 30, RSI at 68.4 and pressing toward overbought, all while still 79.3% below its 12-month high and below its own 200-day line. That is a sharp bounce inside a longer drawdown, not a trend reversal confirmed by the moving averages.

Positioning shows where the crowd's money sits. Funding is cheap on the majors, BTC annualized at 5.1%, ETH at just 1.7%, meaning longs there aren't paying much to hold the bet. It's a different story in SOL, XRP and DOGE, all pinned at 11% annualized funding with long/short account ratios of 2.15, 3.68 and 4.65 respectively: crowded, expensive long positioning. SOL's liquidation tape over its 22-hour window backs this up, $2.28M in short liquidations against just $123k of longs, consistent with its 4.57% day. Open interest remains concentrated in BTC ($2.0B) and ETH ($1.27B), with the altcoins running on a fraction of that capital.

Flow data gives a genuinely constructive read for spot ETFs and a murkier one for exchange balances. BTC ETFs took in $101.7M on 07 Aug, part of a $865.3M net over the last five sessions with all five days pointing the same direction. ETH ETFs added $49.6M on 07 Aug, $243.7M over five sessions, four of five days same-direction. That is real, traceable buying from the traditional-finance side. Whale exchange flows over the last 48 hours tell a different story: a net $302.6M moved onto exchanges, almost entirely an ETH story ($309.7M inflow, zero outflow, the single biggest transfer $165.7M into Coinbase). BTC actually saw a small net $7.1M leave exchanges in that window, despite a $115.2M institutional inflow to Coinbase, because larger sums left Kraken ($118M) and Coinbase ($65.6M). Widen the lens to the last four weekly readings and three of four were net off-exchange (+$445.9M, +$1,075.3M, +$132.2M), with the most recent 48-hour print swinging back negative. That's a reversal inside a choppy series, not a new persistent direction either way. Stablecoin float sits at $306.2B, down 0.75% over 30 days, a mild fade rather than dry powder building.

Sentiment sits at odds with most of the above. Fear & Greed reads 30, labeled Fear, near the top of its own 30-day range of 22 to 33. That gauge looks stale next to five straight days of BTC ETF inflows, mostly bullish MACD readings across the majors, and a total market cap up 0.26% on the day. The crowd calls it fear; the tape shows steady institutional buying and squeezed shorts. Worth watching from here: whether any major reclaims its 200-day line, whether ETH's MACD crosses back above signal, whether funding in SOL, XRP and DOGE cools off its current 11% annualized perch, and whether the next whale flow reading extends the onto-exchange move seen in the last 48 hours or reverts to the off-exchange pattern that dominated three of the prior four weekly prints.
